title: DOM ladder & liquidity heatmap
body:
## Context
CandleViewer's DeepDOM analogue — a clickable price ladder with a time×price liquidity heatmap behind it — is the single densest, highest-frequency surface in the product and the **named first target of the mandatory WebGL engine spike** (`14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-050 "Mandatory WebGL engine spike gate", owner decision #2.2.1). `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.2 schedules this Epic at **S10–S12 of the R2 Order-flow beta train** with 55 points, covering: "Price ladder with bid/ask depth, aggregated size bars, last-trade tape column, position/orders column; rolling-texture liquidity heatmap (`texSubImage2D` newest-column upload) at 200 depth, 100 ms cadence, with a configurable history window; **green = bid, red = ask, user-configurable**; depth aggregation by tick grouping; heatmap↔chart time-axis alignment; liquidity-removal ('pulled orders') shading".

Architecture modules: **M7 Book Engine** (`20-architecture.md` §3.2 — `BookState`, `Resyncer`, `DepthAggregator`, `BookPublisher`, `LiquidityTracker`) and **M9 Order-Flow Engines** (§3.4 — `HeatmapEngine`). The heatmap grid model is already normatively specified in `24-internal-schemas.md` §6 (`HeatmapColumn`, `HeatmapGridSpec`, the `estimated=True` rule during resync, percentile clipping, log default). The transport is already frozen by E17: `book.{symbol}.{depth}` (binary body_kind 1/2) and `heatmap.{symbol}` (binary body_kind 6) in `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1, including the normative `time_bucket_ms` derivation in §6.1.1. The REST backfill contract is `GET /market/heatmap` and `GET /market/orderbook` in `22-api-openapi.yaml`. Persistence is `heatmap_cells` and `orderbook_deltas`/`orderbook_snapshots` in `21-database-schema.md` §4.2/4.3/4.12.

This Epic delivers the **read-only** surface. Click-to-trade (US-DOM-007) and drag-to-amend (US-DOM-008) belong to **E31 Chart & DOM trading interactions** in R3 (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7.2) — E21 ships the interaction *contract* (row hit-targets ≥24 px, `role="grid"` row action menu, the arm-toggle slot) so E31 plugs into it without re-laying out the panel.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories (DOM domain, `11-user-stories.md` §11):** US-DOM-001 (live ladder, Must), US-DOM-002 (liquidity heatmap, Must), US-DOM-003 (adaptive colour scale, Must), US-DOM-004 (trail duration/decay, Should), US-DOM-005 (depth tiers & load shedding, Must), US-DOM-006 (own orders/position on the ladder, Must), US-DOM-009 (deep liquidity scan & book reload, Should), US-DOM-010 (book history backfill on open, Should). Also carries US-MKT-007 (book snapshot+delta) on this surface.

**Screens:** SCR-050 Heatmap + DOM ladder panel, SCR-051 Heatmap & ladder settings dialog, SCR-153 Degraded-mode state (depth-shedding variant only).
**Components:** CMP-108 DomLadderRow, CMP-111 HeatmapCell (logical model + a11y), CMP-113 HeatmapLegend, CMP-122 QuickSizeButtons, CMP-134 DetectorEventCard (mount only), CMP-193 HeatmapOverlay (engine mount point), CMP-227 EstimatedBadge, CMP-229 ArmToggle (visual state only), CMP-230 OwnOrderMarker, CMP-228 PreviewTile, CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner.
**WS topics:** `book.{symbol}.{depth}` (depth ∈ 50/200/500), `heatmap.{symbol}`, `ticker.{symbol}`, `trades.{symbol}`, `orders`, `positions`, `system` (connection_quality).
**REST:** `GET /market/orderbook`, `GET /market/heatmap`.
**Tables:** `heatmap_cells`, `orderbook_deltas`, `orderbook_snapshots`, `orderflow_metrics` (book_imbalance, book_thickness), `chart_presets.heatmap` jsonb.

Engineering total (K + T + S) **62 pts** against the 55-point budget (within ±15%). Design **23**, QA **26**, Security **8** are tracked separately per the capacity rule, for **119** points on the Epic rollup.

## Out of scope
- **Click-to-trade (US-DOM-007) and drag-to-amend (US-DOM-008)** — E31, R3. E21 ships the hit-target/keyboard contract only, with all trading affordances rendered disabled.
- Iceberg / stop-run / absorption detector *algorithms* — E25. E21 only mounts CMP-134 cards and the `(estimated)` badge.
- Liquidation heatmap (`24-internal-schemas.md` §6.4) — E24.
- Replay of the ladder/heatmap — E26 (it reuses these same topics through the one code path).
- Recording the book itself — E16.
- Android / any non-web client.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The DeepDOM surface works end to end
  Given BTCUSDT is recorded and book.BTCUSDT.200 and heatmap.BTCUSDT are live
  When the owner opens SCR-050
  Then a 200-level ladder and a 60-minute heatmap trail render together on one time axis
  And the panel sustains the 100 ms heatmap cadence at >=55 fps with WS->pixel p95 <=120 ms

Scenario: The surface degrades honestly, never silently
  Given frame time exceeds budget for 5 consecutive seconds
  Then the depth tier steps down one rung, a non-blocking notice states why, and a metric records it
  And when the book desyncs the ladder greys with "Book resynchronising" and heatmap columns render as estimated

Scenario: Accessibility parity
  Given a screen-reader user focuses the ladder
  Then every price row is a focusable role=row announcing price, bid size, ask size and own-order size
  And the heatmap exposes a windowed per-level liquidity history table with no colour-only information

Scenario: Epic-level exit
  Then US-DOM-001..006, 009, 010 are Done, zero P0/P1 bugs are open against SCR-050/SCR-051,
  budgets #1 and #14 of 06-performance-and-load-standard.md are recorded as met, the STRIDE model is signed off,
  and axe-core plus one manual screen-reader pass are green on both screens
```

## Technical notes / design
- **Depth identity**: `book.BTCUSDT.50` and `book.BTCUSDT.200` are *independent subscriptions with independent sequences* (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 note). A tier change is a resubscribe + fresh snapshot, never an in-place mutation.
- **Heatmap bucket size** is client-derived per `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1.1 (2–8 device px per column, 3 px target, upward clamp at 1000 ms when `ideal_ms ≤ 2500`), re-derived on resize/DPR change, debounced 400 ms, and answered with `resnapshot: true`.
- **Rolling texture**: newest column only via `texSubImage2D` (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.2; `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.8), fine ring 2048×512×R16F ≈ 2.1 MB plus coarse ring 14400×512 ≈ 14.7 MB (§"Memory").
- **Colour**: green = bid, red = ask (owner decision #10), user-configurable, CVD-safe blue/orange alternative first-class; log scale default; `clip_percentile` normalisation over visible columns (`24-internal-schemas.md` §6.2).
- **Estimated data**: columns produced while the book is `Resyncing` carry `estimated=True`, render at 40% opacity with a hatch, and are excluded from rule-engine liquidity metrics.

## Test plan
Unit/property (book invariants, bucket selection, normalisation), golden-file (heatmap decay/normalisation per `03-testing-strategy.md` §"golden-file"), contract (WS + OpenAPI schema gates), integration (recorded `orderbook_snapshot_delta_*.jsonl.gz` fixtures incl. a seq gap), E2E Playwright incl. pixel-diff golden heatmap frames (`maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01`), perf (engine FPS harness + k6 WS profile), chaos (desync, slow consumer, exchange 5xx), a11y (axe + manual SR).

## Security notes
Primary epic-level threat named by `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.4: **unbounded subscription depth as a DoS vector** — a client subscribing many symbols at depth 500 with a 100 ms bucket can exhaust server CPU/egress. Mitigations: per-connection subscription quotas, `marketdata:read` RBAC on every topic and on `GET /market/heatmap` (`04-security-program.md` §RBAC row 5), the `23-ws-protocol.md` §8.3 connection-quality classifier, and SR-038 (stale books disable trading affordances). Data classification: market data (non-secret) — but own-order/position overlay on the ladder is **account-scoped** and must be RBAC- and scope-filtered.

## Accessibility notes
SCR-050 is explicitly *not* relaxed for density (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §1): `role="grid"` ladder with roving tabindex, ≥24 px row targets, region landmark, windowed heatmap reveal (§6.2), data-table alternative (§6.3), colour never the only channel for bid/ask (§5), and 3:1 contrast at every gradient stop.

## Performance notes
Budget #1 (≤16.6 ms frame at 100k bars + 200-depth heatmap @100 ms) and budget #14 (100 ms cadence sustained, ≤1 dropped/coalesced frame per 10 s) are **hard R1 exit gates re-verified here at R2 scale**; SCR-050 additionally sets a stricter panel budget of WS→pixel ≤120 ms p95 and ≤600 GPU trail frames.

## Observability
Metrics: `heatmap_missing_columns_total` (alert >1%/min), `heatmap_column_publish_latency_ms`, `book_desync_total`, `dom_depth_tier_current`, `dom_shedding_events_total`, `dom_frame_time_ms`. Audit/analytics: `dom.depth_changed`, `dom.settings_changed`, `degraded.entered/exited`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every child Done or explicitly descoped with a recorded disposition.
- [ ] Epic-level AC verified end to end on staging (demo), not just per child.
- [ ] Coverage floors held; zero open P0/P1 against SCR-050/SCR-051.
- [ ] `23-ws-protocol.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `24-internal-schemas.md`, `26-chart-engine-design.md`, `14/15-*` reflect shipped behaviour.
- [ ] WCAG 2.2 AA verified on SCR-050 + SCR-051 (axe CI + manual SR pass).
- [ ] Budgets #1 and #14 recorded; SCR-050 spike-gate evidence attached to the design sign-off.
- [ ] STRIDE finalised, findings triaged, Security sign-off comment present.
- [ ] Epic-level QA regression/exploratory pass recorded (E21-Q06).
- [ ] Demoed to Owner at Sprint Review with acceptance recorded.
- [ ] Retro notes captured as follow-up tickets.

## Sizing
Epic estimate **55 points**, exactly the roadmap sizing for E21 in `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3/§6.2. This is the rollup of the delivery children (Story/Task/Spike): 8+3+2+3+3+2+2+3+2 (S01–S09) + 5+5+2+2+5+2+2 (T01–T07) + 3 (K01) = 55. Design (D01–D08), QA (Q01–Q07) and Security (X01–X03) tickets are tracked on this Epic but, per the roadmap convention, are carried in the cross-cutting design/QA/security capacity lines rather than the epic’s 55-point delivery budget, so they are excluded from this rollup.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E11** (engine core: scene graph, axes, panes, DOM-mirror a11y layer), **E17** (WS transport, binary kinds 1/2/6, `heatmap.time_bucket_ms` contract), **E08** (Bybit adapter, `orderbook.200` ingestion, sequence-gap handling), **E16** (recorder — without recorded book history the heatmap backfill and empty state have nothing to show), **E05** (design system v0 tokens/primitives).
Downstream: **E25** (detectors consume `LiquidityTracker`), **E26** (replay renders this surface through the same pipeline), **E31** (DOM trading plugs into the ladder contract).

## Branch
`feat/e21-dom-ladder-heatmap` as the umbrella convention; each child uses `feat/e21-<short>`. PRs ≤400 LOC diff; the engine texture layer and the React panel must be separate PRs.

title: UX research: how traders read a ladder and a liquidity trail
body:
## Context
SCR-050 is the densest screen in the product and the one with the least prior art inside the team. Before any pixel is drawn we need evidence for four open questions that the screens catalogue leaves to design: (1) how a trader wants the ladder to re-centre (auto-follow vs free-scroll vs lock) without jitter on every tick (US-DOM-001 "Price centring"), (2) whether the heatmap belongs *behind* the ladder, beside it, or behind the chart, and how the two time axes should relate, (3) what "liquidity was pulled" must look like so a trader trusts it, and (4) which of the three depth tiers people actually reach for and what they expect to lose when the app sheds a tier (US-DOM-005).

The Owner and account managers use DeepCharts/DeepDOM and Bookmap-class tools today, so this is comparative research, not greenfield discovery.

## Scope / Deliverables
- 3 moderated sessions (Owner + up to 2 account managers), 45 min, using a scripted clickable harness replaying a recorded BTCUSDT volatile window at depths 50/200/500.
- Competitive teardown of DeepDOM, Bookmap and Sierra Chart DOM: centring behaviour, pulled-liquidity encoding, own-order column placement, legend treatment.
- Probes: "where is real support?", "what just got pulled?", "which row is yours?", "the app just dropped you from 500 to 200 depth — what did you lose?".
- Findings written to `docs/design/research/e21-dom-heatmap.md`: ranked decisions, each phrased as a testable statement a wireframe can satisfy or violate, plus the recommended default for centring mode, trail length and depth tier.
- A recommendation on whether the heatmap and the ladder share one price axis (locked) or can be independently zoomed.

## Out of scope
- Any visual design (greyscale wireframes start in E21-D02).
- Click-to-trade ergonomics — researched in E31's design track.
- Detector card content (E25).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every open question is answered with evidence
  When docs/design/research/e21-dom-heatmap.md is reviewed
  Then each of the four research questions has a recommended default and a named participant rationale

Scenario: Decisions are testable
  Then each adopted decision is phrased so a wireframe reviewer can mark it satisfied or violated, with no purely aesthetic statements

Scenario: Conflicting participant preferences
  Given participants disagree on the centring default
  Then the finding records both positions, names the chosen default, and files it as a setting in SCR-051 rather than silently picking one
```

## Technical notes / design
Harness reuses the E11 benchmark dataset plus one recorded `orderbook_snapshot_delta_*.jsonl.gz` fixture so participants see real liquidity behaviour (walls appearing and vanishing), not synthetic noise. Sessions recorded with consent; notes anonymised in the findings doc.

## Test plan
N/A (research). Validation is the design review: findings presented at the Design Review in Sprint 06 and referenced by E21-D02's sign-off checklist.

## Security notes
Session recordings may contain account balances if the harness shows real data — the harness runs against the demo environment with synthetic account state only. No production keys, no PII beyond participant names, recordings deleted after the findings are accepted.

## Accessibility notes
One session must include a keyboard-only walkthrough of the paper prototype so the `role="grid"` navigation model is pressure-tested before it is drawn.

## Performance notes
N/A (research), but the findings must flag any requested behaviour that would violate budget #14 so it is killed before design, not after build.

## Observability
N/A.

- [ ] Coverage: N/A — no production code.

## Context

title: Motion and reduced-motion spec for the trail, re-centring and resync states
body:
## Context
Three motions on this panel can either help or actively harm a trader: the heatmap trail advancing every 100 ms, the ladder re-centring when price nears the edge, and the transition into/out of "resynchronising". US-DOM-001 requires re-centring "without jitter on every tick"; US-DOM-002 and US-DOM-004 require reduced-motion modes that disable fade animation and use a static decay mode; US-DOM-003 requires colour rescale that is "smooth (no flashing)".

## Scope / Deliverables
- Motion spec in `docs/design/specs/e21-motion.md`: trail advance (continuous scroll vs discrete column step, and the crossover rule by column pixel width), re-centre easing/threshold/hysteresis, colour-scale rescale interpolation duration, resync enter/exit transition, depth-shed notice entry.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` behaviour for each: static trail (no fade), instantaneous re-centre, instant rescale, no notice slide.
- Hysteresis numbers for re-centring (trigger band, target position, minimum interval) expressed so engineering can implement them directly.

## Out of scope
Generic app motion tokens (E05); trading-action motion (E31).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Re-centring does not jitter
  Given price oscillates across the re-centre trigger band
  Then the spec's hysteresis and minimum-interval rules prevent more than one re-centre per the stated interval

Scenario: Reduced motion is complete
  When prefers-reduced-motion is set
  Then every one of the five motions has a defined non-animated equivalent that loses no information

Scenario: Rescale never flashes
  Given the adaptive colour scale rebounds after a liquidity collapse
  Then the spec defines an interpolation that avoids a full-panel luminance jump between frames
```

## Technical notes / design
Trail advance is a texture-space operation (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.8) — the spec must express motion in terms of column steps and sampling offset, not CSS transitions, or it cannot be implemented.

title: Prove the 500-depth heatmap ring buffer and runtime parity
body:
## Context
SCR-050 carries a **mandatory spike gate that blocks design sign-off** (owner decision #2.2.1): the heatmap is the named first target of the engine spike. E06 answered the general question (custom engine viable, ADR-0002/ADR-0011) on candles + footprint. This spike answers the four heatmap-specific sub-questions the screens catalogue enumerates, at R2 scale on the real texture pipeline rather than E06's throwaway prototype:

(a) trail advancing at 100 ms cadence at ≥60 fps at the **200-depth** tier;
(b) a 10-minute sustained run at the **500-depth** tier with no dropped frames — **or** a designed, documented cap that makes 500-depth unavailable with a visible reason in SCR-051;
(c) the full 600-frame GPU ring buffer held inside the per-panel memory budget (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §"Memory": fine ring 2048×512×2 B ≈ 2.1 MB, coarse ring 14400×512×2 B ≈ 14.7 MB);
(d) the same numbers in Chromium, Electron and Tauri/WebView2 — noting that a Tauri failure here does not block sign-off but **locks the shell to Electron** and must be recorded (owner decision #7).

Timebox: **5 working days**, agreed with the Architect.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A harness in `packages/chart-engine/bench/heatmap/` driving `texSubImage2D` newest-column uploads over the E11 benchmark scene (100k bars) at 100 ms cadence, with synthetic 50/200/500-depth column streams generated deterministically from a seed.
- Measured p50/p95/p99 frame time, upload cost per column, texture memory, and dropped/coalesced frame count over 10 minutes, per depth tier, per runtime, on the reference hardware (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §3.1).
- A comparison of column aggregation strategies when >1 column per pixel (max-of-columns preserving spikes, per `26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.6) and of R16F vs R8 quantisation.
- Decision recorded as an amendment/new ADR entry under `docs/plan/27-adrs/` and the evidence attached to the E21-D02 sign-off.
- Follow-up tickets filed for whichever path is chosen.

## Out of scope
Production-shippable code (explicitly a throwaway/promotable prototype); backend column production (E21-T02); the ladder.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: 200-depth budget met
  When the harness runs 10 minutes at 200 depth, 100 ms cadence, in Chromium and Electron
  Then p95 frame time is <=16.6 ms and dropped/coalesced frames are <=1 per 10 s, matching budgets #1 and #14

Scenario: 500-depth decision recorded
  Given the 500-depth tier fails the 10-minute run
  Then a documented cap is specified, SCR-051 shows 500-depth as unavailable with a visible reason,
  and the decision is recorded in an ADR rather than left as tribal knowledge

Scenario: Tauri divergence
  Given Tauri/WebView2 fails the cadence while Chromium and Electron pass
  Then the finding locks the shell to Electron, updates ADR-0011, and does not block E21-D02 sign-off

Scenario: Memory ceiling
  Then retained texture memory for a 600-frame trail at the chosen tier is measured and compared against the
  26-chart-engine-design.md budget, with the MemoryGovernor step-down behaviour exercised at 70% of budget
```

## Technical notes / design
Quantisation to R16F normalised per column max or global scale (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §3.8 flow). DPI is capped at 2 for the heatmap layer to bound texture cost (§3.x DPI note). Eviction: columns outside a 3× viewport window are dropped from GPU buffers and kept in CPU stores until memory pressure. The harness must record per-stage frame markers matching `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3 so a later regression can be stage-attributed.

## Test plan
The harness *is* the test; it is promoted into the CI benchmark suite by E21-Q03 regardless of outcome so the numbers are re-measured every release.

## Security notes
N/A — synthetic data, no network, no credentials.

## Accessibility notes
N/A for the spike itself, but the spike must confirm that maintaining the windowed accessible mirror alongside the texture pipeline does not itself cost frames — measure with the mirror on and off.

## Performance notes
This spike defines the numbers the rest of the Epic is held to: budgets #1 and #14 of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`, plus B4 (heatmap ≤10 ms, upload ≤12 KB/s, texture ≤20 MB) and B5 (combined scene ≤16.7 ms, ≤40 draw calls) of `26-chart-engine-design.md`.

## Observability
Harness emits a machine-readable JSON result consumed by the CI benchmark reporter.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All four sub-questions answered with recorded evidence (numbers per tier per runtime).
- [ ] ADR entry written under `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (a "defer/cap" outcome is itself a recorded decision).
- [ ] Evidence attached to the SCR-050 design sign-off record (E21-D02).
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed for the chosen path.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated for R2 Render performance and R8 Browser/GPU compat.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review.
- [ ] Prototype either promoted (then normal Task DoD applies) or explicitly marked throwaway.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by` E11 (the scene graph, render-pass scheduler and OffscreenCanvas worker this measures against) and E06 (the original engine spike and ADR-0002/0011 it amends).

## Branch

body:
## Context
Two of the standard's **hard gates** live on this surface: budget #1 (≤16.6 ms/frame with 100k bars + 200-depth heatmap at 100 ms) and budget #14 (100 ms cadence sustained, ≤1 dropped/coalesced frame per 10 s). `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §7 also requires the engine benchmark to be a **built-in headless harness** with a seeded synthetic dataset, not ad hoc DevTools profiling, and §9's playbook forbids "open the profiler and guess" as a first step — which only works if stage-attributed frame markers are recorded.

- Outputs p50/p95/p99 overall and per stage, pass/fail against budgets #1/#2/#14, plus a stage-attribution report.
- **k6/Locust WS profile** for the backend side: realistic peak (10 recorded symbols, 5 users, heatmap open on ≥2 symbols) and worst case (all symbols charted everywhere, heatmap+footprint+profile active, plus a 5× volatility burst for 60 s), asserting budget #6 (≤20 ms p95 backend-added latency) and budget #3 (WS tick→screen p95 <100 ms for the heaviest topic set — the R2 hard gate named in `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.3).
- Ingestion soak assertion for budget #5 (zero dropped messages on `orderbook.200` over 24 h) restricted to this Epic's topics.

Fixing regressions (the owning Story's job); E46's product-wide perf hardening in R5; chaos (E21-Q04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  Then a single command produces p50/p95/p99 frame time per stage and a pass/fail verdict against budgets #1 and #14

Scenario: Regression detection
  Given a change increases heatmap texture upload time beyond its 2 ms slice
  Then CI fails and the report names the stage that regressed, without requiring a manual profiling session

Scenario: Backend fan-out under realistic peak
  Given the realistic-peak profile runs for 30 minutes
  Then backend-added latency p95 is <=20 ms and WS tick-to-screen p95 is <100 ms for the heaviest topic set

Scenario: Worst case degrades per policy
  Given the worst-case profile with a 5x burst
  Then the app sheds per ADR-0016 order, the shedding is recorded in metrics, and no message loss is observed beyond detected-and-healed gaps
```

title: Chaos scenarios: desync storms, slow consumers and exchange failures
body:
## Context
`03-testing-strategy.md` requires chaos/failover tests (WS disconnect, exchange 5xx, rate-limit 10018) re-run every release, and `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.4 names E21's own failure surface. The DOM/heatmap is where feed pathologies become visible fastest, which makes it the right place to prove the recovery behaviours rather than discovering them in production.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Chaos harness scenarios, each with a defined expected user-visible outcome and a defined recovery time:
  1. **Sequence-gap storm** — repeated gaps at 1/s for 60 s: book must resync each time, the ladder must show the resync state, heatmap columns must be marked estimated, and no unbounded memory growth may occur.
  2. **Crossed book** injected via a malformed delta: treated as desync, never clamped.
  3. **Upstream WS disconnect** for 30 s: reconnect with backoff, subscriptions restored in priority order, time-to-usable ≤5 s after reconnect.
  4. **Exchange 5xx / rate-limit 10018** on the REST resync path: retries with backoff, user told, no silent stale book.
  5. **Slow consumer**: a client that stops reading — server queue must stay bounded, connection classified `lagging`→`saturated`, heatmap degraded to 1 000 ms, `degraded_topics` announced, and ultimately the documented `slow_consumer` close rather than server memory growth.
  6. **Recorder outage** mid-session: heatmap live continues, backfill reports unavailability honestly.
  7. **GPU context loss**: trail restored from CPU stores; if WebGL2 is unavailable, the documented placeholder appears.
  8. **Clock skew / stalled engine**: `samples=0` columns and the grey-stripe rendering, with `heatmap_missing_columns_total` alerting above 1%/min.

Fixing discovered defects (filed as Bugs); OMS/trading chaos (E45).

  Given any of the eight scenarios runs

  Then each scenario can be re-run by a single documented command and produces the same classification of outcome

Fault injection sits at the fixture/WS-mock layer and at the exchange-adapter boundary, so no production code paths are modified to be testable beyond existing seams. Memory assertions use the same per-symbol accounting as budget #8.

Scenarios are the tests; each has a machine-checkable assertion (metric threshold, state string, recovery time) rather than a human judgement.

Scenario 5 is a direct test of the **DoS vector named for this Epic** (`30-release-roadmap.md` §6.4: unbounded subscription depth) and of protocol goal G4 ("a slow or backgrounded client can never grow server memory"). Every degraded state exercised here must be announced via `role="status"` and readable in greyscale — asserted, not assumed.

Recovery-time targets: ≤5 s time-to-usable after a 30 s outage (SCR-152 performance note); book correct within one snapshot interval after a storm.

## Context
`30-release-roadmap.md` §6.3 exit criterion 10 requires "a11y pass on every new view incl. keyboard-navigable footprint cells and **DOM ladder**" before R2 completes, and `05-accessibility-standard.md` refuses any density exemption for this surface. ## Scope / Deliverables

- **Target size** verification (≥24 px) for ladder rows at each density, with the documented essential-exception reasoning where applicable.

title: Exploratory charter and regression pack for the order-flow DOM surface

## Context
Scripted cases find the failures we predicted; a timeboxed exploratory charter finds the ones we did not. - **Regression pack** assembled for R2 and beyond: the subset of E21-Q02's automated suite plus the manual cases that must be re-run every release, with an execution time budget and an owner.

body:
## Context
US-DOM-001 (Must): *"As an order-flow trader, I want a price ladder with resting bid/ask sizes, so that I can see the book."* This Story builds the ladder half of SCR-050 — the clickable-in-R3, readable-in-R2 price grid that every subsequent DOM feature hangs off. It is the single biggest frontend piece in this Epic because the ladder is simultaneously a high-frequency render surface and a WAI-ARIA grid: `05-accessibility-standard.md` §1 explicitly refuses to relax WCAG for it, and §4.2 names it as the motivating example for roving tabindex ("this prevents 200+ Tab presses to cross a DOM ladder").

Design is signed off in E21-D02/D07; the data contract is delivered by E21-T01 over `book.{symbol}.{depth}`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Screen**: SCR-050 (ladder region, header controls, footer strip). **Stories**: US-DOM-001, and US-MKT-007's presentation on this surface.
- **Components**: CMP-108 DomLadderRow (all variants), CMP-122 QuickSizeButtons (rendered **disabled** — trading ships in E31), CMP-229 ArmToggle (visual state only, locked off), CMP-227 EstimatedBadge, CMP-051 EnvironmentBadge per the per-panel demo/live invariant.
- Columns per the catalogue layout: price · bid size (with size bar) · ask size (with size bar) · last-traded size (tape column) · cumulative depth · own-order column slot (populated by E21-S06) · position marker slot.
- **Virtualised** row rendering — only visible rows in the DOM — driven from the shared-worker-decoded book state.
- **Auto-centring** with the hysteresis from the E21-D05 motion spec: recentre when price approaches the edge, never jitter per tick; `C` = centre on mark, `Space` = recentre and resume auto-follow, `+`/`-` = price step zoom (view-local bindings that shadow the chart's per `05-accessibility-standard.md` §3 precedence rule 3).
- **States**: loading (ladder skeleton) · streaming · stale (dim + "Book stale 3 s") · disconnected (ladder frozen, trading affordances hard-disabled, banner) · resynchronising ("Book resynchronising…" — deltas discarded until a fresh snapshot) · arm-off lock cursor.
- **A11y**: `role="grid"` with `role="row"` rows, roving tabindex, region landmark, `Enter` opens the row action menu, accessible name "64 100, ask 42, own order 0.1 working", ≥24 px row targets at default density, and the §6.3 data-table alternative wired to the same data window.
- Subscription lifecycle: subscribe on mount, unsubscribe with grace on unmount, resync via `resync` frame on sequence gap, re-subscribe after reconnect in priority order.

## Out of scope
Click-to-trade and drag-to-amend (US-DOM-007/008 → **E31**, R3) — affordances render disabled with a lock tooltip. Heatmap (E21-S02). Depth tier control (E21-S05). Own-order data (E21-S06). Detector chips (E25).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Ladder renders
  Given orderbook depth 200 is subscribed for BTCUSDT
  Then price rows show bid size, ask size, last traded size and cumulative depth, updating live
  And updates arrive at up to 20 Hz and each render completes within one frame

Scenario: Price centring without jitter
  Given auto-centre is on and price oscillates around the recentre trigger band
  Then the ladder recentres when price approaches the edge and does not recentre more than once per the specified minimum interval

Scenario: Book resync
  Given a sequence gap invalidates the book
  Then the ladder greys with "Book resynchronising", incoming deltas are discarded until a fresh snapshot applies,
  and normal rendering resumes with no stale rows left behind

Scenario: Stale feed
  Given no book update has arrived for 3 seconds
  Then the ladder dims, shows "Book stale 3 s" with the last-good timestamp, and trading affordances are disabled

Scenario: Keyboard operation
  Given a keyboard user focuses the ladder
  Then one row is in the tab order, arrow keys move the roving focus row to row,
  each focused row is announced with price, bid size, ask size and own-order size, and Enter opens the row action menu

Scenario: Disconnected
  Given the WS transport is down
  Then the ladder is frozen with an explicit banner and no control implies a live price
```

## Technical notes / design
Book state is decoded once in the shared worker (`26-chart-engine-design.md` §"WS client") and read by the panel — the ladder must not decode frames itself. Row identity is the integer `price_ticks` so React keys are stable across recentring; virtualisation keeps the DOM node count bounded (≤60 visible rows at default density per the analogous tape budget). Live updates **patch rows in place** (cell text updated, node identity preserved) so screen-reader focus and any sort state survive (`05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.3 live-data-sync rule). Ambient live-region announcements throttled to the standard default (1 per 2 s, user-configurable) — never per tick.

Error/validation copy comes verbatim from the E21-D07 copy deck.

## Test plan
- **Unit (vitest)**: row projection from book state; cumulative depth computation; centring hysteresis with a fake clock; stale/resync/disconnected state machine; virtualisation window maths.
- **Storybook interaction**: every CMP-108 variant; keyboard roving-tabindex traversal; `Enter` row action menu; disabled trading affordance tooltip.
- **Contract**: consumes the `BookSnapshot`/`BookDelta` schemas from `ws-schemas.json`; a schema drift fails CI.
- **Integration**: fixture-driven book stream including a seq gap; assert the resync state renders and clears.
- **E2E (Playwright)**: open SCR-050 on the demo env, assert live row updates, force a gap, assert the resync banner, assert keyboard traversal and announcements via the DOM mirror.
- **A11y**: axe-core zero serious/critical; manual NVDA/VoiceOver pass recorded.
- **Perf**: ≥55 fps with 200 visible rows (US-DOM-001 NFR); WS→pixel ≤120 ms p95 for this panel.
- Coverage ≥80% frontend.

## Security notes
SR-038 is directly implemented here: while a book is rebuilding or stale, DOM trading affordances are disabled for that symbol — the R2 version renders them disabled anyway, but the *state plumbing* that E31 will depend on is built and tested now. The panel must never present a frozen price as live. ## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA: 1.4.11 (non-text contrast for size bars), 2.1.1/2.1.2 (keyboard, no trap), 2.4.3 (focus order), 2.4.7/2.4.11 (focus visible/not obscured), 2.5.8 (target size ≥24 px), 4.1.2/4.1.3 (name/role/value, status messages). Grid pattern per WAI-ARIA APG. Data-table alternative per `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.3 including the "no longer in view" banner.

## Performance notes
Budget: ≥55 fps at 200 visible rows, panel WS→pixel ≤120 ms p95 (stricter than the global 250 ms), virtualised DOM. React re-renders must stay off the hot path — row updates go through a per-symbol high-frequency store, not component state.

title: Render the liquidity heatmap surface with legend, empty state and accessible reveal
body:
## Context
US-DOM-002 (Must): *"I want historical resting liquidity rendered as a heatmap behind the ladder and chart, so that I can see where liquidity sat and vanished."* E21-T05 built the engine layer; this Story mounts it in SCR-050, wires the subscription, renders CMP-113 HeatmapLegend, implements CMP-111's **logical model and accessibility contract** (the catalogue's explicit CMP-111/CMP-193 responsibility split puts the data shape and a11y here, the texture there), and handles the two states that are pure product behaviour: the no-recorded-history empty state and the estimated/resyncing rendering.

Colour convention is locked by owner decision #10 (green = bid, red = ask), user-configurable, with the legend always stating the active convention.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Subscribe `heatmap.{symbol}` with the client-derived `time_bucket_ms` per the normative algorithm in `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1.1: one column SHOULD occupy 2–8 device pixels, 3 px target, **upward clamp at 1000 ms whenever `ideal_ms ≤ 2500`**; re-derive on pane resize, DPR change and `window_seconds` change; send `ctl { time_bucket_ms }` **debounced 400 ms**; discard state on `resnapshot: true`.
- Mount CMP-193 behind the ladder and (when the panel is chart-hosted) behind the price pane, sharing the time axis.
- **CMP-113 HeatmapLegend**: ramp with numeric anchors, active convention statement, linear/log indicator, adaptive-vs-locked indicator.
- **Empty state** (US-DOM-002 scenario 3): when the recorder has no book history for the symbol, show an explicit empty state offering to start recording, deep-linking to the recorder screen.
- **Estimated rendering**: columns with `estimated=true` at 40% opacity with the hatch; a missing column (`samples=0`) as a vertical grey stripe; both explained in the legend/tooltip, never colour-only.
- **Edge gutters** rendering `off_window_bid_qty` / `off_window_ask_qty` so the user knows depth exists beyond the visible price window (`24-internal-schemas.md` §6.2 step 4).
- **Accessible windowed reveal** (CMP-111 contract, `05-accessibility-standard.md` §6.2): focus a ladder row → documented key → "liquidity history at this level" as a sparkline plus data table for that price, with values as numbers.
- Cursor/hover readout carrying side and numeric size (non-colour channel per `26-chart-engine-design.md` §"Non-colour encodings").

## Out of scope
Scale/palette controls (E21-S03), trail length (E21-S04), backfill of older history (E21-S08), settings dialog (E21-S09), the texture pipeline itself (E21-T05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  Given the book has been recorded for the last 20 minutes

  And it is aligned to the same time axis as the ladder and the chart

Scenario: Colour convention configurable
  When the convention is inverted in settings
  Then every heatmap surface updates consistently and the legend states the active convention

Scenario: No recorded book

  Then the heatmap area shows an explicit empty state offering to start recording, and no misleading blank grid

Scenario: Estimated columns are visibly estimated
  Given the book was resyncing for part of the window
  Then those columns render at reduced opacity with a hatch and are described as estimated in the accessible readout

Scenario: Bucket re-derivation
  Given the pane is resized so the ideal bucket changes
  Then the client re-derives the bucket, sends ctl debounced by 400 ms, discards state on resnapshot and rebuilds without a visible tear

Scenario: Accessible reveal
  Given a keyboard user focuses a ladder row and presses the documented reveal key
  Then a table of that price level's liquidity history over the window is presented with numeric values
```

## Technical notes / design
Bucket derivation is normative and unit-tested by `heatmap_bucket_selection` (the test name is fixed by `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1.1 — the ladder clamp is asserted there). Frames are decoded once in the shared worker and transferred to the render worker without a copy. Reduced motion disables the fade animation and uses the static decay mode (US-DOM-002/004 NFRs).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: `heatmap_bucket_selection` (all rungs, the ≤2500 ms clamp, DPR variations); estimated/missing column classification; edge-gutter totals; empty-state predicate.
- **Storybook**: CMP-113 variants (linear/log, adaptive/locked, both conventions, CVD-safe), CMP-111 windowed-reveal output, empty state.
- **Contract**: `HeatmapColumn` schema + binary kind 6 decode.
- **Integration**: fixture stream with a resync window; assert estimated rendering and recovery.
- **E2E**: open the panel on a recorded symbol, assert the trail renders and the legend matches the active convention; open an unrecorded symbol, assert the empty state; resize the pane and assert exactly one debounced `ctl`.
- **Visual**: Playwright golden heatmap frames, `maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01`.
- **A11y**: axe on the reveal output; manual SR pass on the reveal path.
- Coverage ≥80% frontend.

## Security notes
`marketdata:read`; a rejected subscription must render a permission state. The empty state's "start recording" action must respect RBAC — a `viewer` sees the explanation without the action (recording is an owner/manager capability per `04-security-program.md`). No user-supplied string reaches the shader or the topic name unvalidated (symbol comes from the instruments cache).

## Accessibility notes
Implements all three mandatory layers for this surface: DOM mirror (engine root), windowed accessible tree (§6.2 — the binding constraint CMP-111 owns), and the data-table alternative (§6.3). Bid/ask never colour-only: column/axis-side convention + text label + focus readout. Reduced-motion path required.

## Performance notes
Budget #14: 100 ms cadence sustained at 200 depth, ≤1 dropped/coalesced frame per 10 s; ≤600 GPU trail frames for this panel; the accessible reveal must build lazily on demand — it may not maintain a live table for every price level.

title: Adaptive, locked and logarithmic colour-scale controls
body:
## Context
US-DOM-003 (Must): the heatmap scale must adapt to current liquidity so it stays informative across regimes, must be lockable to absolute values with the lock indicated, and must offer a logarithmic mapping that keeps small and large resting sizes distinguishable — with the legend always showing the active bounds and mapping. E21-T06 built the LUT/scale pipeline; this Story exposes it in the product: the header quick control on SCR-050, the legend's live bounds, and the lock affordance.

## Scope / Deliverables
- SCR-050 header `scale [log v]` control: log / linear with gamma, and adaptive / locked.
- Percentile-window configuration surfaced (the `clip_percentile` of `HeatmapGridSpec`) with a sensible default and an explanation of what it does in plain language.
- Legend (CMP-113) updates live with the numeric bounds, the mapping type and the adaptive/locked state.
- Lock affordance: locking freezes the bounds at their current values (editable as absolute numbers), with an unmistakable locked indicator that is not colour-only.
- CVD-safe palette selectable here as well as in SCR-051, per US-DOM-003's NFR ("CVD-safe palette available").
- Persist the choice per symbol/panel into the workspace layout state and `chart_presets.heatmap` jsonb (`21-database-schema.md` — "colour scale, trail decay, bid=green/ask=red").

## Out of scope
The scale/LUT implementation (E21-T06); the full settings dialog (E21-S09); trail length (E21-S04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Adaptive scale
  Given liquidity drops by an order of magnitude
  Then the colour scale rescales using the configured percentile window and the legend shows the new bounds

Scenario: Fixed scale
  When the user locks the scale to absolute values
  Then it stops adapting, the bounds remain editable as numbers, and the locked state is indicated by text and icon, not colour alone

Scenario: Log scale
  When logarithmic mapping is chosen
  Then small and large resting sizes remain visually distinguishable and the legend states the log mapping

Scenario: Persistence
  Given the user sets log + locked bounds and reopens the workspace
  Then the same scale settings are restored for that symbol/panel

Scenario: No flashing on rescale
  Given the scale rebounds after a liquidity collapse
  Then the transition is smooth, and instantaneous under prefers-reduced-motion
```

## Technical notes / design
Changing the scale is a uniform/LUT update (≤1 frame) and must **not** drop the historized frame buffer (SCR-051 Performance note) — the UI must therefore not unmount or resubscribe the layer on a scale change. Bounds display uses the instrument's size precision from the instruments cache, not raw floats.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: control state machine (adaptive↔locked), bounds editing validation, persistence round-trip through the preset schema.
- **Storybook**: legend across mapping × adaptive/locked × palette × theme.
- **E2E**: switch to log, lock, reload the workspace, assert restoration; assert no resubscribe occurs on a scale change (network assertion).
- **A11y**: axe; the locked state must be in the accessible name; manual SR check of the legend.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
Settings persist to the user's own preset row — writes must be scoped to the authenticated user and validated server-side against the preset schema (no arbitrary jsonb).

## Accessibility notes
`05-accessibility-standard.md` §5: locked/adaptive and log/linear conveyed by text, never by colour or a bare icon; numeric bounds are readable text, not only a gradient; the CVD-safe palette is a first-class option reachable from this control.

## Performance notes
Scale change ≤1 frame; no re-subscription; no loss of the retained trail.

## Observability
`dom.settings_changed {key: heatmap.scale|heatmap.locked|heatmap.palette}` analytics; `heatmap_scale_mode` gauge.

title: Trail duration, decay mode and the client memory guard
body:
## Context
US-DOM-004 (Should): the trader controls how much liquidity history the trail shows (5 s–600 s per SCR-051's validation range, with the roadmap's "configurable history window" extending to the 60-minute case in the Epic goal), can disable age-based decay entirely, and — crucially — is told when a requested trail would exceed the client memory budget rather than being allowed to crash the panel. The NFR is explicit: *"memory per symbol bounded and displayed in the performance panel."*

## Scope / Deliverables
- SCR-050 header `trail [60s v]` control and the SCR-051 trail field (5–600 s), plus decay mode: smooth / none (static).
- **Decay off** renders intensity as true size with no age-based fading; the static mode is also what `prefers-reduced-motion` selects.
- **Memory guard**: compute the retained-frame cost for the requested trail at the current depth tier and bucket; if it exceeds the client budget, clamp the request and explain the maximum for the current depth tier in plain language (US-DOM-004 scenario 3) with an offer to reduce depth instead.
- Per-symbol heatmap memory reported into the performance panel (SCR-155-class surface owned by E10/E46 — this Story publishes the metric, it does not build the panel).
- Trail changes reuse the retained ring where possible: shortening the trail must not force a re-snapshot; lengthening beyond the retained window triggers backfill via E21-S08 rather than a blank region.

## Out of scope
The backfill fetch itself (E21-S08); ring implementation (E21-T05); depth shedding (E21-S05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Trail length
  When the trail is set to 5 minutes
  Then only the last 5 minutes of book history render, and the time axis labels agree with that window

Scenario: Decay off
  When decay is disabled
  Then intensity reflects true size with no age-based fading, and the same static mode is used automatically under prefers-reduced-motion

Scenario: Memory guard
  Given a requested trail would exceed the client memory budget at the current depth tier
  Then the request is clamped, the maximum for that tier is explained in plain language, and reducing the depth tier is offered as the alternative

Scenario: Shortening is free
  When the trail is shortened
  Then no re-snapshot is requested and the retained columns are simply windowed

Scenario: Memory is visible
  Then per-symbol heatmap memory is published and readable in the performance panel
```

## Technical notes / design
Cost model: retained columns = `trail_seconds * 1000 / time_bucket_ms`; bytes ≈ columns × rows × 2 B (R16F) per ring, checked against the `26-chart-engine-design.md` memory budget (fine ring 2.1 MB, coarse ring 14.7 MB reference figures). The guard must use the *actual* current tier and bucket, not defaults, or the explanation will be wrong.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: cost model across tiers/buckets; clamp threshold boundaries; shortening path asserts no resubscribe; reduced-motion selects static decay.
- **Storybook**: the clamp explanation message for each tier.
- **E2E**: set an oversized trail, assert the clamp message names the correct maximum for the active tier.
- **Perf**: memory measured at the maximum permitted trail per tier and compared with the model's prediction (model error must be within a documented tolerance).
- **A11y**: the clamp message is announced via `role="status"` and is reachable without pointer.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
The guard is a client-side resource-exhaustion control; the server-side counterpart (`window_seconds` ≤900, 2 000-column snapshot cap) lives in E21-T02. Neither may be the only defence — this Story must assume the server could return more than requested and still not exceed its own budget.

## Accessibility notes
Clamp explanation is text, announced politely, with the alternative action reachable by keyboard. Static decay is the reduced-motion default, per `05-accessibility-standard.md` and US-DOM-002/004 NFRs.

## Performance notes
Bounded per-symbol memory is the point of this Story; the MemoryGovernor step-down at 70% of budget (E21-T05) remains the backstop.

title: Depth tiers 50/200/500 with automatic load shedding and pinning
body:
## Context
US-DOM-005 (Must), owner-facing: *"I want to choose depth tier 50/200/500 and have the app shed depth under load, so that responsiveness is preserved."* Its NFR is the one that makes this Story non-negotiable in character: **"shedding decisions logged and exposed as metrics; never silently degrade without telling the user."**

Two independent controllers can reduce fidelity: the client's frame-budget watchdog (US-DOM-005: frame time over budget for 5 consecutive seconds → step down one rung) and the server's connection-quality classifier (`23-ws-protocol.md` §8.3: `lagging`/`saturated` → throttle multipliers, forced coalescing, `degraded_topics`). E21-T07 records the combined policy as ADR-0016; this Story implements it and is the reason that ADR exists.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Depth control on the SCR-050 header (`depth [200 v]`) and in SCR-051; the active tier always shown on the DOM header.
- Tier change = resubscribe `book.{symbol}.{depth}` (new subscription identity, fresh snapshot) with the designed 1–2 s rebuild state, never a frozen-looking panel.
- **Automatic shedding**: frame time over the budget for 5 consecutive seconds → step down one rung (500→200→50), following the ADR-0016 rung order (heatmap cadence and trail are shed before depth); restore one rung when load allows, with the ADR's hysteresis and minimum dwell time so it cannot oscillate.
- **Non-blocking notice** explaining why, via CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner / the SCR-153 depth-shed variant: what was reduced, why, what still works, and how to pin.
- **Manual pin**: pinning prevents automatic shedding entirely and is clearly indicated; the app must then say what it does instead when it still cannot keep up (per ADR-0016).
- Reaction to the server-side signal: on `system` `connection_quality` with this panel's topics in `degraded_topics`, show the same vocabulary rather than a second, competing message.
- 500-depth availability gated on E21-K01's outcome: if capped, SCR-051 shows the tier as unavailable **with a visible reason** (the catalogue's own fallback wording) and the `heatmap_depth_500` feature flag governs it.

## Out of scope
The server's classifier (E17), the ADR text (E21-T07), the banner's visual design (E21-D03), backend depth caps (E21-T01).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Tier selection
  When depth 200 is selected
  Then the corresponding topic is subscribed, a fresh snapshot arrives, the rebuild state is shown briefly,
  and the tier is displayed on the DOM header

Scenario: Automatic shedding
  Given frame time exceeds the budget for 5 consecutive seconds
  Then the tier is reduced one step, a non-blocking notice explains why, a metric and a log entry are recorded,
  and the tier restores when load allows after the minimum dwell time

Scenario: Manual override
  When the tier is pinned
  Then automatic shedding will not change it, the pin is clearly indicated,
  and if the app still cannot keep up it says so rather than silently dropping frames

Scenario: No duplicate or contradictory messaging
  Given the server reports the connection as saturated while the client is also shedding
  Then exactly one coherent explanation is presented to the user, per ADR-0016

Scenario: 500-depth capped
  Given the engine spike capped the 500 tier
  Then SCR-051 presents 500 as unavailable with a visible reason and the feature flag state is respected

Scenario: Never silent
  Given any automatic reduction occurs
  Then a user-visible explanation, a metric increment and a structured log entry all occur; none may be omitted
```

## Technical notes / design
Frame-budget watchdog reads the engine's frame-marker instrumentation (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.3) rather than a naive rAF timer, so shedding is attributed to real render cost. Thresholds (5 s trigger, dwell time, hysteresis band) are named constants imported from a single module and asserted against the ADR-0016 values in a test, so doc/code drift fails CI. Tier change discards heatmap state too, because `depth` invalidates the heatmap subscription identity as well (`23-ws-protocol.md` §5.4).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: watchdog trigger/restore with a fake clock (exactly 5 s, 4.9 s, oscillating input); rung order; pin behaviour; ADR-constant agreement test.
- **Storybook**: banner variants for each shed reason and direction.
- **Integration**: simulated `connection_quality: saturated` frame → assert single coherent message.
- **E2E**: throttle the renderer (CPU throttling in Playwright), assert step-down, notice, metric, and restoration.
- **Perf**: verify that after shedding, frame time returns inside budget on the reference hardware.
- **A11y**: banner is `role="status"`, announced once, readable in greyscale; pin state in the accessible name.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
Shedding must never disable or obscure a safety signal — the stale-book indication, the demo/live badge and the disabled-trading state keep full fidelity at every rung (ADR-0016 invariant, SR-038). A user-pinned 500-depth tier across many symbols is also the client side of the DoS concern in `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.4; the client must respect the server's per-connection deep-book subscription cap and surface the rejection clearly rather than retrying in a loop.

## Accessibility notes
`role="status"` banner naming exactly which capability is degraded and what still works, in plain sentences (SCR-153 A11y); per-panel badges repeat the specific degradation in their accessible name; nothing about shedding is conveyed by colour alone.

## Performance notes
This Story *is* the enforcement of budgets #1/#14 at runtime. Shedding order per `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4.4 as reconciled in ADR-0016.

## Observability
Metrics: `dom_depth_tier_current{symbol}`, `dom_shedding_events_total{reason,direction}`, `dom_frame_time_ms` histogram, `dom_tier_pinned`. Analytics/audit: `dom.depth_changed`, `degraded.entered{cause,sheddedFeatures}`, `degraded.exited{durationMs}`.

title: Own-order and position column on the ladder against the reconciled-OMS contract
body:
## Context
US-DOM-006 (Must): *"I want my working orders, stops and average entry shown on the ladder, so that I manage in the book."* Its NFR is a correctness rule with real money behind it: **"own-order overlay never derived from optimistic UI state alone — always reconciled with exchange truth."** Multi-account is in scope from day one because CandleViewer fans one ticket out to N accounts as a trade group: per-account markers aggregate per row with a count, expandable to per-account detail.

In R2 there is no OMS yet: E29 (OMS core) and E28 (trade groups) land in R3 (S14+), **after** this Epic's train window (S10–S12). This Story is therefore scoped to what can be completed inside R2 with no R3 blocker: the own-order/position **column, projection contract and rendering**, fed by the `OwnOrderProjection` port whose only R2 implementation is a fixture/demo adapter. No R3 ticket is a blocker; the live OMS adapter is wired in R3 by E31 (which already depends on E29/E28), consuming this Story's contract unchanged. E31 later attaches drag and click behaviour to exactly these markers.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CMP-230 OwnOrderMarker** in the ladder's own-order column: working limit size and an identifying glyph per row; stop orders distinguished from limits; reduce-only indicated.
- **Position marker**: average entry row highlight and the position's side/size, plus the liquidation-price row marker when available.
- **Multi-account aggregation**: per-row count badge with expandable per-account detail (trade-group aware, per `24-internal-schemas.md` trade-group model).
- **`OwnOrderProjection` port** (`24-internal-schemas.md`): a versioned, read-only interface (rows keyed by `price_ticks`, side, size, kind, reduce-only, account id, confirmation state) with two R2 adapters — a deterministic fixture adapter for tests/Storybook and a demo-environment adapter reading the account-scoped WS `orders`/`positions` topics where they already exist. The R3 OMS adapter is out of scope here.
- **Reconciliation rule**: markers are rendered from reconciled OMS state; when an order is filled or cancelled externally, the marker clears **within 1 second** of the private WS event or the next reconciliation tick. No marker may exist that is derived only from a local optimistic action.
- Stale-marker safety: if the private feed is down, markers are shown with an explicit "not confirmed" treatment rather than being silently trusted or silently hidden.
- Accessible name extension: the row announcement includes own-order size and side ("…, your buy order 0.5 at this price"), and the per-account detail is keyboard-reachable.

## Out of scope
Placing/amending/cancelling from the ladder (US-DOM-007/008 → E31); the OMS itself (E29); trade-group construction (E28); **binding the projection port to live OMS/trade-group state — that wiring belongs to E31 in R3**; the order ticket (E30).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Markers
  Given a working limit at 63,400
  Then that row shows the order size in the dedicated own-order column with an identifying glyph
  And the row's accessible name includes the own-order side and size

Scenario: Multi-account
  Given a trade group has orders at several prices
  Then per-account markers aggregate per row with a count, expandable to per-account detail, reachable by keyboard

Scenario: Stale order
  Given an order was filled or cancelled externally
  Then the marker clears within 1 second of the private WS event or the next reconciliation

Scenario: Never optimistic-only
  Given a local action has been sent but not acknowledged
  Then any marker shown is visibly marked pending and is removed if reconciliation does not confirm it

Scenario: Private feed down
  Given the orders/positions feed is disconnected
  Then existing markers are marked unconfirmed with the last-good timestamp, and the panel does not imply live order state

Scenario: RBAC scoping
  Given a manager who may see only a subset of accounts
  Then only that subset's orders and positions appear, and the aggregate count reflects only permitted accounts
```

## Technical notes / design
Marker state is a projection delivered by the `OwnOrderProjection` port (backed in R3 by the reconciled OMS store), keyed by `price_ticks` so it lines up with ladder rows exactly. Aggregation groups by row then by account; the expansion is a popover, not an inline row expansion, so ladder row heights stay uniform for virtualisation. Own-order markers must never be obscured by heatmap intensity — this is an explicit SCR-050 sign-off item and is why the column is dedicated rather than an overlay glyph.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: projection from OMS state; aggregation and count; pending/unconfirmed state machine; clearing within the 1 s budget with a fake clock.
- **Storybook**: CMP-230 variants (single, aggregated, pending, unconfirmed, stop vs limit, reduce-only).
- **Integration**: private-feed fixture with an externally-cancelled order; assert marker clearing.
- **E2E**: demo-environment order placed via the API through the demo adapter, marker appears; cancel externally, marker clears within 1 s. Contract tests pin the `OwnOrderProjection` shape so the R3 OMS adapter is a drop-in.
- **Security test**: a manager restricted to one account must not receive or render another account's markers — asserted at both the API and UI layers.
- **A11y**: axe; keyboard path into the per-account detail; SR announcement includes own-order info.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
This is the one part of E21 that renders **account-scoped, financially sensitive** data, so `04-security-program.md` §8's cross-Kind rule applies and the `security` label is mandatory. Threats: (a) **broken object-level authorisation** — the `orders`/`positions` topics must be filtered server-side by account scope, never client-side; a hand-crafted subscription must not yield another user's orders; (b) **stale/spoofed state** leading a trader to believe an order exists when it does not — mitigated by the reconciliation rule and the unconfirmed treatment; (c) information disclosure through the aggregate count (the count must not reveal the existence of orders in accounts the user cannot see). Data classification: financial, account-scoped. Abuse-case checks are covered by E21-X02.

## Accessibility notes

- Pulled-liquidity shading on the heatmap surface for levels removed without matching prints (the "pulled orders" shading named in the Epic's roadmap scope), also `(estimated)`.
- **Info popover** with the fixed caveat copy from the E21-D07 copy deck: no L3 data, replenishment inferred from L2 only.
- Accessible readout: band values as a small data table, reload events as a list with numeric values and timestamps — not colour or glyph alone.

## Out of scope
The detection algorithms (E21-T04); the iceberg heuristic and its confidence score (E25); alerts/rules on these events (E40/E35 — they consume the same bus events).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin

  Then a panel shows cumulative bid and ask depth within each configurable distance band and their difference, updating live

Scenario: Reload detection
  Given a level is consumed and replenished within the configured window
  Then a reload event is flagged with an "(estimated)" badge and the replenished size

Scenario: No MBO caveat
  Then the info popover states that without L3 data replenishment is inferred from L2 changes only

Scenario: Estimated is never dropped
  Given a reload event is rendered anywhere (row marker, detector strip, accessible list)
  Then the estimated marking is present in every one of those places, including the accessible name

Scenario: Resyncing book
  Given the book is resynchronising
  Then no new reload or pulled markers appear, and the panel says why rather than showing stale numbers
```

Band definitions come from SCR-051 and are expressed in ticks or bps from mid; the panel must render the instrument's own precision. `(estimated)` appears in the accessible name, not only as a visual chip; band values are available as text; the caveat popover is keyboard-reachable and dismissible with Esc.

Low-frequency panel (≤1 Hz effective); must not add to the ladder's frame cost and must not trigger ladder re-renders.

title: Progressive book-history backfill when a symbol is opened
body:
## Context
US-DOM-010 (Should): *"I want the heatmap to load recent recorded book history when I open a symbol, so that context is immediate."* The live subscription only carries the most recent 2 000 columns (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1.1); everything older is REST (`GET /market/heatmap`, built in E21-T03). Three behaviours matter: progressive newest-first loading with a progress indicator, an explicitly marked boundary when only partial history exists, and prompt cancellation with memory release when the user switches symbol. The NFR requires backfill to run **off the interaction path** with first useful paint ≤1 s.

## Scope / Deliverables
- On symbol open (and on trail lengthening beyond the retained window), fetch history in chunks newest-first up to 24 hours or the configured trail, whichever is smaller.
- Progress indicator that does not block interaction: the live trail is usable immediately while history fills in behind it.
- **Partial history**: load what exists and mark the boundary with the first available timestamp (a visible edge marker plus an accessible description), never an ambiguous blank.
- **Cancellation**: switching symbol or closing the panel aborts in-flight requests promptly (AbortController through to the fetch layer) and releases the decoded buffers; assertable in tests.
- Chunk decode and texture upload on the worker path, never on the main thread.
- Respect the server's disclosed effective resolution (downsampled segments) by labelling the affected region rather than rendering it as native-cadence data.
- Empty case delegates to E21-S02's empty state (offer to start recording).

## Out of scope
The REST endpoint (E21-T03); recording (E16); replay seek (E26).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Backfill
  Given up to 24 hours of recorded book history exists
  Then opening the symbol loads it progressively, newest first, with a progress indicator
  And the live trail remains interactive throughout

Scenario: Partial history
  Given only 3 hours exist
  Then 3 hours load and the boundary is marked with the first available timestamp, described accessibly

Scenario: Cancel
  When the symbol is switched during backfill
  Then the load cancels promptly, in-flight requests are aborted, and the decoded buffers are released

Scenario: First useful paint
  Given a recorded symbol is opened
  Then a useful heatmap is painted within 1 second, before backfill completes

Scenario: Downsampled segment disclosed
  Given part of the requested window is beyond the downsample boundary
  Then that region is labelled with its effective resolution rather than presented as native-cadence data
```

## Technical notes / design
Chunking strategy: request newest window first at the active bucket, then walk backwards; each chunk is decoded off-thread and pushed through `pushHeatmapColumn` into the coarse ring. Backfilled columns must be reconcilable with live columns at the join without a duplicate or gap — key on bucket start timestamp and make the merge idempotent.

Memory interacts with E21-S04's guard: backfill may not push retained memory past the clamp; it stops early and says so.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: chunk planning; join/merge idempotency at the live boundary; abort propagation; effective-resolution labelling.
- **Integration**: partial-history fixture; assert the boundary marker's timestamp equals the first available column.
- **E2E**: open a recorded symbol and assert first-useful-paint under 1 s with the progress indicator visible; switch symbols mid-load and assert no further network activity and no memory growth.
- **Perf**: backfill must not degrade live frame time — assert frame time during backfill stays inside budget.
- **A11y**: progress is announced politely (not per chunk); the boundary marker has a text description.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
The client must treat REST responses as untrusted input: validate matrix/axis dimension agreement before uploading to a texture (a mismatched `row_count` is the out-of-bounds risk also guarded in E21-T05). Requests carry the session credential; aborted requests must not leave the token in a retry loop. Rate: concurrent backfills are capped client-side to avoid becoming the DoS source described in `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.4.

## Accessibility notes
Progress uses a polite live region with throttled updates; the partial-history boundary is described in text; nothing about load state is colour-only.

## Performance notes
First useful paint ≤1 s; backfill strictly off the interaction path; decode and upload on workers; frame budget preserved during load.

## Observability
`heatmap_backfill_client_duration_ms`, `heatmap_backfill_chunks_total`, `heatmap_backfill_cancelled_total`, `heatmap_first_paint_ms`.

## Context

US-SET-005 (settings persistence) and US-DOM-003/004/005/010 all land here.

## Scope / Deliverables
- The dialog per the catalogue layout and the E21-D03 hi-fi: depth tier (50/200/500), colour scale (log/linear + gamma), trail length (5–600 s) + decay mode, palette (bid/ask swatches + CVD-safe set), row height (10–40 px), centre lock / auto-follow, show-toggles (own orders, position, prints, cumulative depth, queue estimate with `(estimated)`), qty presets, "confirm market orders in LIVE", detector toggles + sensitivity.
- **CMP-228 PreviewTile** (`kind: "heatmap"`) live preview on sample data.
- **Validation**: trail 5–600 s; row height 10–40 px; at least one qty preset; inline errors with the copy-deck wording.
- **Cost disclosure**: measured bandwidth/CPU figure per depth tier shown next to the control.
- **Resubscribe notice** on depth change with the 1–2 s rebuild state.
- **Reset to defaults** per tab and for the whole dialog.
- Persistence into the user's preset (`chart_presets.heatmap` jsonb and the per-user settings key space, e.g. `recorder.default_depth`-style dotted keys in `user_settings`), scoped to the authenticated user.
- 'Preview with colour-vision simulation' toggle on the Colour tab.

## Out of scope
Trading behaviour behind the "Trading" tab's controls (E31 consumes these settings); detector algorithms and their sensitivity semantics (E25 — this Story renders the controls and persists the values against the agreed schema).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All controls present and validated
  Then depth tier, colour scale, trail, palette, row height, centre lock, show-toggles, qty presets and detector toggles
  are all present, and out-of-range values are rejected inline with the specified message

Scenario: Live preview
  When a colour or scale setting changes
  Then the preview tile updates without a live subscription and without dropping the running heatmap's frame buffer

Scenario: Cost disclosure
  When the depth tier is raised
  Then the measured bandwidth and CPU cost for that tier is shown before the change is applied

Scenario: Resubscribe notice
  When the depth tier is changed
  Then the dialog states the book will resubscribe and the panel shows the 1-2 s rebuild state rather than appearing frozen

Scenario: Persistence and reset
  Given settings are changed and the app is restarted
  Then the settings are restored for that user; reset-to-defaults restores the documented defaults and says which ones changed

Scenario: Keyboard and screen reader
  Then every control is a labelled form field with units, reachable and operable by keyboard, with numeric colour stops available as text inputs
```

## Technical notes / design
Settings apply to the running panel without rebuilding it except where the contract requires a resubscribe (depth, price grouping, bucket). Colour/scale changes are uniform updates (≤1 frame). Validation ranges are single-sourced constants shared with the backend preset schema so client and server cannot disagree.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: each validation rule at its boundaries; reset-to-defaults diff; persistence round-trip; "no resubscribe on colour change" assertion.
- **Storybook**: every tab, every error state, the CVD-simulation preview.
- **E2E**: change each setting, assert the running panel reflects it and that a reload restores it.
- **A11y**: axe; keyboard-only completion of every tab; SR labels include units.
- **Contract**: the persisted payload validates against the preset schema server-side; an invalid payload is rejected.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Accessibility notes
All controls labelled with units; the colour-scale editor exposes numeric stops as text inputs alongside the gradient widget; the CVD-simulation toggle is itself an accessibility feature and must be keyboard-reachable; dialog focus trap with Esc dismissal and focus return.

## Performance notes
The preview tile uses static sample frames, never a live subscription; applying settings must not drop the historized frame buffer.

title: Book engine: depth tiers, tick aggregation and the ladder publisher
body:
## Context
Module **M7 Book Engine** (`20-architecture.md` §3.2) already exists in skeleton form from E08 (L2 reconstruction, sequence-gap detection). This Task completes the three components the ladder needs: `DepthAggregator` (level-aggregated views: raw, 1-tick, N-tick bucketed), `BookPublisher` (snapshot at subscribe/resync, deltas thereafter, conflated to 50 ms for the ladder topic and 100 ms for the heatmap topic) and the depth-tier negotiation that makes `book.{symbol}.{depth}` real for depth ∈ {50, 200, 500}.

The transport contract is frozen by E17 and must be implemented exactly: `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 puts **depth in the topic name, not the options**, because depth changes the identity of the state — `book.BTCUSDT.50` and `book.BTCUSDT.200` are independent subscriptions with independent sequence numbers. Binary body kinds 1 (`book_snapshot`) and 2 (`book_delta`) are already specified in §3.4, including the 16-byte snapshot trailer carrying Bybit's `xu`/`xseq`.

Upstream cadences are fixed by Bybit (`24-internal-schemas.md` §2.2): depth 1 @ 10 ms, 50 @ 20 ms, 200 @ 100 ms, 500 @ 200 ms. v1 subscribes 200 for heatmap/DOM and 1 for best bid/ask. **Depth 1 is snapshot-only and is re-sent every 3 s even when unchanged** — the engine must not treat an unchanged depth-1 resend as a book event or the heatmap shows phantom columns. That is a named trap and needs a test.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/backend/book_engine/aggregator.py` — `DepthAggregator.aggregate(bucket_ticks, depth)` producing bucketed level views; buckets keyed on integer `price_ticks` (constraint C5 in `24-internal-schemas.md` §1 — floats produce phantom levels).
- `packages/backend/book_engine/publisher.py` — `BookPublisher.publish()`: emits `BookSnapshot` on subscribe and on resync, `BookDelta` thereafter, conflated to ≤50 ms (ladder) / ≤100 ms (heatmap); levels that fall outside the subscribed depth are emitted with size `0` so the client window stays exactly `depth` levels per side (`23-ws-protocol.md` §7).
- Depth-tier subscription manager: one upstream Bybit subscription per (symbol, depth) actually demanded, fanned out to N clients; unsubscribe grace window; ≤10 args per Bybit subscribe request (E08 budgeting).
- `Resyncer` completion: on gap, negative qty, or **crossed book** (best bid ≥ best ask — treated as desync, never clamped), drop the local book, emit `BookDesyncEvent`, resubscribe, buffer deltas, replay those with seq > snapshot seq.
- Binary encoder for kinds 1 and 2 wired to `packages/protocol` from E17.
- `BestQuoteEvent` emission for the DOM header (`24-internal-schemas.md` §3: bid, bid_qty, ask, ask_qty, spread_ticks, spread_bps, mid).
- Metrics and structured logs (see Observability).

## Out of scope
Heatmap columns (E21-T02); REST backfill (E21-T03); liquidity bands/refill detection (E21-T04); any frontend.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Independent depth subscriptions
  Given a client subscribes book.BTCUSDT.50 and book.BTCUSDT.200 on one connection
  Then two subscriptions exist with independent sequence counters and independent snapshots
  And each receives exactly its own depth of levels per side

Scenario: Level leaving the window
  Given a level previously inside the subscribed depth falls outside it as the top of book moves
  Then that level is sent once with size 0 and never again, so the client window stays exactly depth levels per side

Scenario: Crossed book is a desync, not a clamp
  Given applying a delta produces best bid >= best ask
  Then the engine drops the book, emits BookDesyncEvent, resubscribes and sends a fresh snapshot
  And it does not emit any conflated delta derived from the crossed state

Scenario: Depth-1 keepalive is not a book event
  Given the depth-1 topic re-sends an unchanged snapshot after 3 seconds
  Then no BookDelta, no BestQuoteEvent change and no heatmap sample are produced from it

Scenario: Conflation cadence
  Given upstream deltas arrive at 20 ms on the 50-depth topic
  Then outbound ladder frames are emitted at most every 50 ms, each carrying the merged final state, losing intermediate frames but never final state
```

## Technical notes / design
Levels held in two `SortedDict`s keyed by `price_ticks`; book memory 500 levels × 2 sides × 32 B ≈ 32 KB/symbol (`20-architecture.md` §3.2). State machine `INIT → SNAPSHOT_PENDING → LIVE → DESYNCED → SNAPSHOT_PENDING`; **`LIVE` is the only state from which derived engines consume** — E21-T02 depends on this invariant to set `estimated=True`. Conflation uses the coalescing policy of `23-ws-protocol.md` §8.2 (last-write-wins per level, whole-frame merge). Decimal↔tick conversion per constraint C5: `price_ticks = round((price - price_origin) / tick_size)`, integer form derived, Decimal authoritative.

Error codes: an unknown depth in a topic name returns `invalid_topic_format` (`23-ws-protocol.md` §10).

## Test plan
- **Property (hypothesis)**, per `03-testing-strategy.md` §"Book engine": book never negative-size after any valid delta sequence; snapshot fully resets state; replaying the same delta sequence twice from the same snapshot yields identical state; a delta with `seq` ≤ last-applied is a no-op or triggers resync; malformed/duplicate deletes do not crash.
- **Unit**: aggregation at bucket_ticks ∈ {1, 5, 25}; zero-size eviction at the depth boundary; depth-1 keepalive suppression; crossed-book detection; conflation cadence with a fake clock.
- **Integration**: replay `orderbook_snapshot_delta_*.jsonl.gz` fixture including the seeded `seq` gap and out-of-order delivery; assert exactly one `BookDesyncEvent` and a correct post-resync book.
- **Contract**: binary kind 1/2 round-trip against `ws-schemas.json` (E17's `ws_message_schemas` CI gate).
- Coverage ≥85% line / ≥75% branch on `book_engine`.

## Security notes
Subscription authorisation is `marketdata:read` (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6 permission table; `04-security-program.md` RBAC row 5) and is checked server-side on every subscribe — a hand-crafted raw frame must not bypass it. Depth-500 subscriptions are the DoS surface named in `30-release-roadmap.md` §6.4: this Task enforces a per-connection cap on concurrent (symbol, depth≥200) subscriptions, configurable via `ws.max_deep_book_subs` (default 4), returning a typed error rather than silently accepting. Book data itself is non-secret market data.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend.

## Performance notes
Budget #5 (sustain `orderbook.200` at 100 ms with zero dropped messages), budget #6 (≤20 ms p95 backend-added latency from book update to outbound frame) and budget #8 (≤300 MB resident per recorded symbol) of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`. Per-symbol asyncio task isolation so one symbol's burst cannot starve another.

## Observability
Metrics: `book_desync_total{symbol,depth}`, `book_apply_latency_ms`, `book_publish_latency_ms`, `book_subscriptions_active{depth}`, `book_crossed_total`. Logs: structured desync event with `prev_update_id`, `got_update_id`, `resync_count`. Event `BookDesyncEvent` on bus topic `sys.md.desync` (`24-internal-schemas.md` §3).
